description: Forgejo Actions runner lane policy for EdgeVector local forge. Merge-blocking ci-required stays on the docker/pc + macos-arm64 merge gate; heavy compute (fold workspace clippy) runs on the dedicated PC docker lane; release/deploy jobs use the Mac host lane via the macos label.

merge_gate.purpose: Pre-merge ci-required only. Keep capacity free for fold/lastgit PR gates.
merge_gate.notes: Mac merge runner is host-only macos-arm64 after 2026-07-13; PC owns docker/* merge jobs. Do not attach long release/deploy workflows to these labels.

heavy.purpose: Long-running non-gating work. Heavy compute (fold full-workspace clippy) runs on pc-heavy-runner, a dedicated PC docker lane that can never occupy merge-gate slots. Release/deploy jobs (fold tags, exemem-infra deploys) stay on the Mac host runners via the macos label. Never a required pre-merge status.

workflow_routing.example: heavy-clippy.yml: runs-on: heavy (PC docker). release.yml / deploy jobs: runs-on: macos (Mac host). Leave ci-required needs: limited to merge-gate jobs only.

heavy.notes: Since 2026-08-18 the heavy label lives on pc-heavy-runner (PC docker, capacity 2, CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=16 storm cap) — the Mac host lane missed heavy-clippy's 12m cap even uncontended (run 5587) while the PC clears it in ~2min (run 5588). mac-forge-runner-host declares macos only; re-adding heavy:host there is a deliberate fallback decision, not a default. When the PC is down, heavy jobs queue (the lane is non-gating). Host-mode Mac runners stay capacity 1 so a release does not stack with another long job.

proof.expected: heavy_ok=true, merge_gate_has_heavy=false; --live additionally sees global runner pc-heavy-runner on label heavy
